items.readme:
# Xbox2Windows

Xbox2Windows researches static recompilation from Xbox Series X|S (Scarlett) to x64 Windows. It translates selected x64 machine code into C++ and selected gfx1013 shaders into desktop DXIL. The public tests build their own inputs and run without a game installation.

**Startup status.** Source-built Windows programs run from entry to process exit. The main executable was absent from the inspected package. Execution of the title's CPU code, full-game startup and frame rate remain unverified.

[Results](#current-results-and-open-work) · [Coverage chart](#instruction-coverage) · [Community and contributions](#community-and-contributions) · [Build on Windows](#first-build) · [Choose an experiment](#choose-an-experiment) · [Run the GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check)

## Current results and open work

| What runs | What was compared |
|---|---|
| **x64 programs from PE entry** | A two-record archive reader runs with blast 1.3 decompression under Windows, the PE mapper and the recompiled build. The three agree on output bytes, callback order, completed records, allocations, releases and exit status, including truncation and a refused output window. [Reproduce the archive comparison](docs/experiments.md#recompiling-the-blast-decoder) |
| **Raster draw from PE entry** | The shim-startup EXE renders the 64x64 test triangle offscreen. The native, mapped and recompiled runs agree on all 16,384 RGBA bytes and exit 42; a mirrored variant and an unknown draw case exercise the negative controls. [Reproduce the draw comparison](docs/experiments.md#exe-startup-through-the-desktop-runtime-shims) |
| **Pixel shaders** | At `c849f7a`, 851 of 12,101 PS records compiled, built D3D12 pipelines and matched controlled output on RTX 4060 Laptop and WARP. A two-mip draw verifies explicit LOD 0. A separate probe follows a constant-buffer read shared by 529 blocked records. Swapping buffers changes all 1,024 probe pixels. [Color readback](docs/experiments.md#offline-pixel-shader-recompilation) · [Depth and bindings](docs/experiments.md#buffered-depth-export) · [Read probe and latest counts](docs/experiments.md#first-unresolved-constant-buffer-read) |
| **Compute shaders** | Of 2,689 package records, 12 ran under the tested UAV bindings. Each adapter passed 14 full-buffer comparisons, including dispatches with different group counts. [Dispatch and readback](docs/experiments.md#compute-uav-stores-from-a-native-container) |
| **Mesh shaders** | A specialized entry fetched indexed vertices from a GPU buffer. Two position sets covered 1,024 and 276 pixels on a 32×32 target, matching the CPU reference on hardware and WARP. [Mesh draw and specialization limits](docs/experiments.md#single-group-mesh-entry-specialization) |
| **Windows runtime** | Bink frame-buffer allocations reach the Windows heap through the shared provider. The FidelityFX experiment follows scratch writes from two passes through the RCAS output on an 8×4 tile. [Allocation, failure and retry](docs/experiments.md#frame-buffers-through-the-shared-windows-heap) · [Upscaler pixel comparison](docs/experiments.md#last-writers-of-the-pass-26-scratch-reads) |

### Instruction coverage

The chart counts instruction forms exercised by passing source-built fixtures. The experiments above measure program outputs and package shader records.

![Instruction forms exercised by the latest published Windows CI fixtures](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/refs/heads/coverage-dashboard/dashboard.svg)

Both Windows jobs on `main` must pass before CI publishes a new chart. The image shows the measured commit and run ID.

[Chart source commit and CI run](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/tree/coverage-dashboard#instruction-coverage) · [Find forms without a passing fixture](CONTRIBUTING.md#share-a-reproducible-finding)

## Community and contributions

- **Claim a task.** Search for the behavior or test name in [open issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues) and [open PRs](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/pulls). On the issue, say what you will test, on which platform, and which shared interface or other PR your work depends on. For a first patch, start with [good first issues](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22).
- **Submit a change.** Keep the PR focused on one behavior. Link the task it advances and any prerequisite PR. Include the exact command, expected and observed results, and a negative control for a new fixture. [Patch and evidence guide](CONTRIBUTING.md#submit-and-review-a-patch)
- **Review a PR.** For CPU translation or PE loading, reproduce the comparison with the original fixture. For shaders or GPU compatibility, check the DXIL and relevant WARP or hardware results. Both reviewers cover shared CPU/GPU interfaces. Record your verdict and the commit you tested. The Maintainer merges after review threads are resolved and the required Windows check passes. [Review responsibilities](CONTRIBUTING.md#who-reviews-and-merges-a-pr)
- **Contribute a hardware result.** Run the [standalone GPU check](#run-the-gpu-check) and post the report in [issue #1](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1). You can also claim a batch there without owning a GPU. Verify the original logs, add new adapters as rows in the [hardware table](#hardware-coverage), and link driver retests in the existing row.

[New contributor guide](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/75) · [Build and debugging Q&A](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/discussions/categories/development-q-a) · [Report a bug or propose research](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/new/choose) · [Community conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) · [Private security reports](SECURITY.md)

## First build

On x64 Windows, install Python 3.11 or newer and Visual Studio's **Desktop development with C++** workload, including x64 MSVC, CMake, Ninja, and Windows SDK 10.0.26100 with DXC. Windows CI uses Python 3.12. Open PowerShell at the repository root and run the following commands.

```powershell
.\tools\dev.ps1
python -m venv out/pe-env
.\out\pe-env\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -r requirements-dev.txt
cmake --preset dev
cmake --build --preset dev
ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R 'desktop_root_signature|era_heap_allocation|offscreen_warp'
```

The smoke tests exercise a D3D12 root signature, heap allocation and software rendering. For just those checks, you can omit the two Python setup commands. With the Python environment installed, [run a focused experiment](#choose-an-experiment) or run the full suite with `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error`.

To build and test at /O2 as Windows CI also does, use the `release` preset in place of `dev`. Its build directory is `out/build/release`.

Contributing from macOS or Linux? See the [non-Windows host guide](docs/non-windows-hosts.md) for the platform-independent Python and LLVM 15 checks.

### Windows build notes

- **DXC validation.** `shader_metadata_probe` skips when the validator lacks module-only validation. DXC 1.8.2502 is the first verified release that passes. To use a separate DXC installation, configure with `cmake --preset dev -DDXC_EXECUTABLE=C:/path/to/dxc/bin/x64/dxc.exe`. [Results by release](docs/experiments.md#module-only-validation-by-dxc-release) · [Original report](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/98) · [DXC download](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases/tag/v1.8.2502)
- **Windows 10.** The source-built BVH buffer operations run on in-box WARP at SM 6.0. For WARP checks that require SM 6.5 or DXR, use the app-local Agility SDK and WARP packages. [BVH buffer operations](docs/experiments.md#bvh-buffer-operations-on-in-box-warp) · [Windows 10 setup](docs/experiments.md#windows-10-with-the-app-local-agility-sdk-and-warp)
- **Independent build.** A Windows 11 contributor reproduced the three smoke tests from a clean checkout at `71bb9f4` and again after an incremental rebuild at `2465837`. [Toolchain, full-suite results and capability skips](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/2#issuecomment-7063351821)

## Choose an experiment

After the full [Windows build](#first-build), run one comparison from the repository root.

| Experiment | Focused test |
|---|---|
| Native, mapped and recompiled archive reader | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_archive_blast$' -V` |
| Indexed mesh draw on WARP | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^mesh_indexed_draw_warp$' -V` |
| Compute shader buffer writes on WARP | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^compute_store_aot_warp$' -V` |
| PE 32/64-bit base fixups against Windows | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_native_highlow$' -V` · [scope and controls](docs/experiments.md#highlow-and-mixed-width-base-relocations) |

The control-flow CPU translator supports [source-built string memory transfers](docs/experiments.md#string-memory-transfers-in-the-control-flow-cpu-lifter). MOVS and STOS, with and without REP, copy and fill 1-, 2-, 4- and 8-byte elements in either direction.

### Tests by area

| Area | A contribution you can verify | Focused CTest command |
|---|---|---|
| Static CPU recompilation | Compare leaf, chained-range and cross-function translations with their source-built originals and negative controls, including [Bink frame plane requests](docs/experiments.md#frame-plane-requests-in-binkallocateframebuffers) and the [Bink group descriptor builders](docs/experiments.md#grouped-allocation-descriptor-builders). | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^cpu_' -V` |
| Script states | Reproduce a parent/child lookup, an ambiguous selection or a damaged sibling link with a synthetic tree. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^script_(state_literals\|path_links)$' -V` |
| Resource metadata | Check a [relocated resource root](docs/experiments.md#relocated-resource-root) against its block directory and type schema. | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^resource_relocated_root$' -V` |
| Texture recovery | Check a packed mip tail, a first refill byte, the fields of a generated BC7 block, or a resident mip drawn on the software adapter. [Look up a texture key across archives and inspect a matching descriptor](docs/experiments.md#reading-logical-ranges-and-probing-structured-resources). | `ctest --preset dev --no-tests=error -R '^(bcpack_prefix_and_mip_tail\|bc7_block_reference\|bc7_draw_warp\|resource_range_controls)$' -V` |

## Run the GPU check

Download the [Windows x64 GPU check and SHA-256](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/releases/tag/gpu-check-v0.1.0), verify and extract the ZIP, then run this in PowerShell from the extracted folder. The package contains its own shaders and needs no compiler, console or game files.

```powershell
.\Run-GpuCheck.ps1
```

With a package built from current source, use `.\Run-GpuCheck.ps1 -Adapter Radeon` to select a hardware adapter by part of its name. For source builds, set `XBOX2WINDOWS_ADAPTER` before running CTest.

On the RX 570, vkd3d-proton exposes Shader Model 6.6, so forced wave64 ran where the Windows row skips at Shader Model 6.5; the BVH differential skipped at DXR tier 0. A [GTX 750 Ti](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/1#issuecomment-7080565902) also reported a 32-lane maximum and skipped forced wave64; its BVH differential skipped at DXR tier 0. The RX 570 and GTX 750 Ti reports show DXVK's placeholder driver 35.0.65535.65535 in the adapter line and name the physical card in the comment.

An earlier batch at commit `def386a` covered seven GPU models in eight community reports. Each Radeon completed all 38 forced-wave64 groups with zero mismatches. The RX 9070 XT, RTX 3070 and RTX 5070 driver retest reported zero D3D12 debug warnings and errors in their passing checks.

Maintainers link independent results to the original report and record the adapter, driver, commit and outcome. Names or handles are added on request. The hardware-report and independent-build milestones are complete. The remaining community milestone is a fix verified by the contributor who reported the problem.

</details>

## Case study and provenance

The installation metadata inspected for this case study lists a Scarlett executable. The main executable was absent from the inspected files. The public regression suite uses source-built fixtures and independently built shaders. [Intake methods and evidence](docs/experiments.md#static-executable-intake)

Windows Authenticode verification on the local copy reported `HashMismatch` for 12 DLLs and `NotSigned` for four. Three independently compared whole-file SHA-256 values matched the community reports. The cause of the digest mismatch and the original signing path remain undetermined. [Methods and fingerprints](https://github.com/R0Y00/Xbox2Windows/issues/52)

items.readme: # Xbox Emulator **Running the Xbox Series X|S library on PC. A continuation of [drycheetah84/TomBox](https://github.com/drycheetah84/TomBox).** The runtime reimplements the console's platform layer (Xbox-flavoured Direct3D 12, precompiled RDNA2 shaders, unified-memory textures, system libraries) so dumped, already-decrypted Xbox Series X|S builds run as normal Windows processes. It is not tied to any single title. This repo tracks our continuation — new titles brought up, platform calls extended, shader stages unlocked. Uses legally obtained, already-decrypted dumps. The runtime does no key extraction or package decryption. **Source code:** the emulator's Rust workspace is in this repo: [`crates/`](crates/), [`tools/`](tools/) and `Cargo.toml`. It contains no game files, binaries or build output. **Contributing:** pull requests are welcome, especially console library functions still marked missing in the [library map](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md). See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Licensed MIT OR Apache-2.0. ## Status [![system functions](docs/img/badge-imports.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![Direct3D 12.x methods](docs/img/badge-d3d12x.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![RDNA2 instructions](docs/img/badge-instructions.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![shaders translated](docs/img/badge-shaders.svg)](#tested-titles) [![shader stages](docs/img/badge-stages.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) [![milestones](docs/img/badge-milestones.svg)](#milestones) [![titles examined](docs/img/badge-titles.svg)](#tested-titles) [![Xbox console libraries](docs/img/badge-console.svg)](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md) [![progress map](docs/img/progress.svg)](docs/img/progress.svg) One square per item. The first four sections use upstream's definitions so the numbers stay comparable: green = done, amber = partial (a stub, a forwarder, or not verified to work), grey = not done — imported system functions of the Fortnite EXE, Direct3D 12.x interface methods, RDNA2 shader instructions the decoder knows, and the eight shader stages (mesh and amplification still grey). The fifth section is ours and covers Xbox console libraries only: the exports of the console OS DLLs (EmbeddedXvd of every analysed title, union, so the newest console OS sets the surface) that no same-named DLL in a PC's C:\Windows\System32 exports, so console-only DLLs (d3d12_xs, xg_xs, xmem, AcpHal, chad, xapu, xcrdapi, the *legacy variants, ...) count in full and modified PC DLLs (kernel32, advapi32, mfplat, ...) only for their console-only exports, plus the GDK wrappers the emulator redirects; plain Windows DLLs (ntdll, msvcrt, ucrtbase, combase, ...) are not shown. Coloured implemented / forwarded / stub / missing; lighter squares are functions an analysed title imports. Per-title import coverage likewise counts only imports from console libraries. Generated by tools/progress/gen.py; per-function tables in docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md, headline numbers in tools/progress/summary.json. ## Milestones Counted live by `tools/progress/gen.py`; full table with evidence in [docs/MILESTONES.md](docs/MILESTONES.md). | Milestone | State | |---|---| | All imported system functions covered (671/671) | done | | Full title shader sweep translated (105,506/105,506) | done | | All Direct3D 12.x methods covered | in progress (map) | | All RDNA2 instructions verified | in progress (map) | | All shader stages (Mesh, Amplification) | in progress (map) | | All Xbox console libraries covered | in progress (map) | | Fortnite boots, first frames, login, hotfix, mode select, BR lobby | done (7 run milestones) | | 3D scene correct | not reached | | Keyboard / controller input | not reached | | Audio | not reached | | Gameplay | not reached | | A second title running | not reached | ## Tested titles | Title | Build | Result | |---|---|---| | Fortnite (Chapter 2 Season 4) | 2.0.1461.7919 | Boots, logs in to a private server, reaches the lobby. 2D interface correct. 3D scene lit but the character material is wrong and bloom shows artifacts. No audio. Not playable. On this machine (2026-11-21): boots, first frames, window on the primary monitor, login complete, hotfix success, game-mode select, Battle Royale lobby (`UI.State.Athena.Frontend`). | | XDefiant | dump examined | **Not run.** Imports and console OS (10.0.22000) mapped in [docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md](docs/LIBRARY_MAP.md); new modules include XCurl, Bink2Scarlett, chad (XDsp*), xapu (XApu*). | | Grand Theft Auto VI | 1.0.2.1 | **Not run** (dump has no executable). # WinRust **A Windows shell written in Rust: faster and lighter than the stock one.** Small native programs (no .NET, no Electron) that replace parts of Windows: the taskbar, File Explorer, file search, Task Manager, plus a disk cleaner, a disk map and a photo viewer. One installer puts them in, one button takes them all out. English | [Русский](README.ru.md) | [日本語](README.ja.md) | [Português (Brasil)](README.pt-BR.md)

> **Read this first.** WinRust turns off Windows Search, hides the taskbar and can turn off Explorer as the shell. The exe is not code-signed, so SmartScreen will warn you. A restore point is created before install, but try it on a spare machine or a VM first. ## Install 1. Download `WinRust.exe` from the [latest release](https://github.com/Lemxy/WinRust/releases/latest) (Windows 10/11, x64). 2. Run it as administrator. 3. Tick the components you want and press the install button. On a fresh install, `rust-explorer` is unchecked. Tick it to replace the Windows Explorer shell (or use the gear on the topbar row: the **Shell: rust-explorer** switch). They are installed in the right order; one that fails or is skipped does not stop the others, the window lists what went wrong. Windows Search is optional: on a stripped Windows (for example a debloated LTSC image without the Windows Search service) that step is skipped with a warning instead of failing the install. If UAC asks for **another administrator's** password, the per-user settings (startup entries, scheduled tasks, PowerShell profile, search permissions) still go to the user who is signed in, not to the administrator you typed. If the installer cannot tell who that is, it stops before changing anything. **Automatic updates:** after the first install, a `WinRust-update` scheduled task (runs as SYSTEM, no UAC prompt) checks the latest release at boot and once a day. It downloads only the programs that changed, checks each file against a manifest signed with the project's key (a tampered or unsigned release is refused) and replaces only files that are already installed. A running program switches to the new version the next time it starts (sign-in or reboot). Log: `%ProgramData%\plugin-launcher\install.log` (`autoupdate:` lines). To turn it off, disable the `WinRust-update` task in Task Scheduler; **Remove all** deletes it. **Manual update:** download the new `WinRust.exe` from the releases page, run it as administrator and select the components you want to update or install. An existing `rust-explorer` stays selected by default for updates. Your settings and the saved original Windows values stay. The installer is in English. The language button in its corner (or the gear on the bar → **Bar settings → Language**) switches every WinRust program to the chosen language: English, Русский, 日本語 or Português (Brasil). The choice is stored in `%ProgramData%\WinRust\lang.txt` (`en`, `ru`, `ja`, `pt`). ## Remove - **Remove all** in the installer window undoes everything: Windows Search, the taskbar, Explorer and the services come back. - One plugin at a time: `plugin-launcher uninstall ` (see [Command line](#command-line)). - **If the screen is left without a taskbar or desktop:** press Ctrl+Alt+Del → Task Manager → Run new task → `explorer.exe`, then run the installer and press Remove all. On uninstall, `rust-explorer` restores the service startup values and the svchost grouping threshold saved before installation. Older installs without those backups keep their current values and report a warning. ## What gets installed | Plugin | What you get | What it changes in Windows | |---|---|---| | **rust-search** | File search over all NTFS drives, Alt+Space. With topbar, Win+R opens its Run mode: history, folder completion (Tab), Ctrl+Shift+Enter runs as administrator | Disables the Windows Search service, blocks SearchHost.exe, hides the taskbar search box | | **rtaskmgr-win32** | Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc opens it) | `taskmgr.exe` is redirected to it (the system file is untouched). Also installs the **rs-du** disk cleaner. The **Speed** page has opt-in, reversible switches: Game / Work profiles (stop background services, close launchers or sync apps, start them again), clear the memory standby cache (now, or automatically while topbar runs), block the Windows Start menu, widgets and Phone Link processes, one weekly `winget upgrade` instead of third-party updaters, Defender exclusions for build caches and game libraries, faster NTFS (no last-access times, no 8.3 names), an ad-blocking hosts file. **Startup** also lists logon/boot tasks and third-party auto-start services, with how much each slowed the last boots (Windows' own boot log). **What's slow** shows driver time (DPC/interrupts), hung windows, slow disk and boot times. Uninstall turns all of it back | | **topbar** | A Windows 11-style bottom bar: windows, clock, volume, menus | Hides the stock taskbar. Also installs **reshell** (hotkeys: Win+Ctrl+1/2/3 and Win+\` switch desktops (Win+1..9 open the bar's app buttons), Win+D shows the desktop, Win+I opens Settings, Win+E the file manager; brings the taskbar back if the bar dies), **rs-du**, and a block in your PowerShell profile (`zoxide`, `grep`=rg, `ll`=eza, `cat`=bat; does nothing if they are missing). The gear menu has short pages: Theme, Colors and transparency (any colour of the bar and the WinRust windows, the bar's opacity), Templates (save your own looks and switch between them), the bar (bottom / left / right edge, size, auto-hide, buttons at the left end like Windows 10) and Reset everything to defaults | | **rust-explorer** | A file manager with tabs, and the desktop | Folders and drives open in it; **Explorer stops being the shell** (comes back by itself if topbar fails). On fresh installs, adjusts the startup settings of InventorySvc, lfsvc and DoSvc, and the svchost grouping threshold, when their values can be backed up. Its own copier (several files at once on SSDs, unbuffered for big files, progress in the status line) and right-click **Compress to ZIP** (all cores) / **Extract here** (ZIP and 7z), our own ZIP engine; a `.zip` opens like a folder (browse, copy out, open files from it). "Show in folder" from other programs selects the file (for the common folders: Downloads, Documents, Desktop, Pictures, Music, Videos and pinned ones, also when no window is open); the mouse back / forward buttons work; right click the desktop to hide its icons. Requires topbar | | **wiztree** | A disk-usage map ("WinRust Disk" in Start) | Nothing, apart from the file and a shortcut | | **photoview** | A fast photo viewer | Adds it to "Open with" (it does not become the default) | | **rust-settings** | Settings in Rust: display (resolution, refresh rate), sound (volume), power plan and drive space, per-app volume and device choice, night light, display arrangement by dragging, network adapters, Wi-Fi on every adapter (password or 802.1X), VPN and proxy, Bluetooth, apps, Windows Update, disk cleanup, theme, about | Nothing, apart from the file and a shortcut. Win+I and the bar menus open this window instead of Windows Settings (only a few rare pages still open the system ones) | | **debloat** | Off: telemetry, diagnostics, Copilot, Recall, Start ads, Edge in the background | Services and registry policies; old values are saved and restored on uninstall. **Command line only:** `install debloat --yes` | | **purge** | Removes the bundled junk like Tiny11 does: Clipchamp, News, Weather, Xbox overlays, Teams, Cortana, Widgets, Skype and more, plus telemetry tasks | **IRREVERSIBLE, no undo.** Apps are removed for all users and from the image; the Store, Settings, Start and runtimes stay. Run `purge.exe` first: it only lists. **Command line only:** `install purge --yes` (OneDrive and Edge: `purge.exe --apply --onedrive --edge`) | | chrome-rs | A browser | Not installable yet | Every change is reversible: uninstall puts back the values that were there before. ## Styles The gear at the left end of the bar opens **Bar settings**; a style picked on its **Theme** page applies at once to the bar, the file manager (rust-explorer) and the search window (Alt+Space): | Style | Look | |---|---| | **Normal** | Windows 11 blue, the bar at the bottom | | **Terminal** | Green on black, Consolas, square corners | | **Floating dock** | A pill-shaped bar in the middle; maximized windows get the whole screen, the dock slides away over them and comes back at the bottom edge | | **Tiling** | A thin bar at the top, amber accent, rounded like Normal; "Tile the windows" puts the open windows side by side | | **White road** | Light ivory with gold: faint low-poly triangles, some traced in gold, behind the bar, its panels and rust-settings | | **Ruby** | Deep garnet with a bright ruby accent: a smooth top-to-bottom gradient with a soft gloss, behind the bar and its panels | | **Windows 98** (BETA) | Classic grey with a navy accent, square corners, Tahoma. Colours, corners and font only: no 3D bevels yet | | **Windows 7** (BETA) | Aero-like glass blue with white text | The gear menu also sets the bar position (bottom, left or right: a side bar shows icons only and the panels open next to it) and auto-hide. The choice is stored in `%ProgramData%\WinRust\style.txt`. ## Benchmark One-off measurements on one machine (Windows 11 IoT Enterprise 10.0.26300, RTX 4060 Laptop, NTFS). Treat them as orders of magnitude, not lab numbers. | What | Windows | WinRust | Difference | |---|---|---|---| | File search (rust-search over all of C: vs `dir /s` over one folder) | 8,340 ms | 45 ms | **99.5%** faster | | Same vs `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` | 16,200 – 28,600 ms | 45 ms | **99.7–99.8%** faster | | Open a folder window (rust-explorer, median of 5 runs) | 420 ms | 60 ms | **86%** faster | | Shell memory (topbar + rust-explorer + rs-shell + reshell vs explorer.exe) | 366 MB | 46 MB | **87%** less | | Same, plus the search index (53 MB) | 366 MB | 99 MB | **73%** less | | File manager binary size (now with ZIP and 7z inside) | 3,280 KB | 1,179 KB | **64%** smaller | | Task manager binary size | 5,791 KB | 954 KB | **84%** smaller | | Idle CPU of the bar (topbar after optimization, % of one core) | 0.00–0.10% (explorer) | 0.05–0.10% | on par with Explorer | | Copy 5,000 small files, ~160 MB (rust-explorer: IFileOperation, Explorer's engine, vs its own copier) | 16.3 s | 2.3 s | **86%** faster (7x) | | Copy one 1 GB file (same) | 0.58 s | 0.60 s | equal | | Pack the same 5,000 files into ZIP (`Compress-Archive` vs rust-explorer's Compress to ZIP) | 48.4 s | 0.75 s | **98%** faster (64x) | In short: **64–99% faster or smaller in the size/speed tests, equal on idle CPU and on copying one big file.** Caveats: rs searches a ready-made MFT index (it pays 53 MB of memory for that), while `dir` and PowerShell walk the disk from scratch; explorer.exe was still running with its windows during the test, so the memory gain is slightly overstated; Windows Search and the stock Task Manager were not compared. The copy and ZIP runs (`cargo test -p rust-explorer --release bench -- --ignored`) were single runs on data that was just written, so both sides read from the memory cache; our ZIP was slightly bigger (0.9 MB vs 0.7 MB) because each file is compressed on its own core. ## Screenshots **Taskbar** ![Taskbar on the desktop](docs/screenshots/taskbar.webp) ![Taskbar menu](docs/screenshots/taskbar-menu.png) ![Bar menu, new look](docs/screenshots/topbar-menu-new.png) **Task Manager** (Russian UI) ![Task Manager](docs/screenshots/task-manager.webp) **File manager** ![File manager](docs/screenshots/explorer.png) --- ## For developers ### Layout ``` src/ the installer (plugin-launcher.exe) main.rs the plugin table PLUGINS: name, texts, install/uninstall pair, icon install/ what each plugin changes and how it is undone (one file per plugin) cli.rs, ui.rs the command line and the window; both call the same install functions common/ winrust-common: language switch (t!/tf!: English, Russian, Japanese, Brazilian Portuguese), UI styles and palettes, reg.exe output parser, NTFS MFT reader plugins/ sources of every plugin, each its own crate ReShell/ reshell (desktop hotkeys, topbar safety net), ships with topbar payload.txt the exes embedded into the installer, and where the build puts them payload/ those exes once built (not in git) scripts/ build, update, release ``` Everything is one cargo workspace (one `Cargo.lock`, every exe in `target\release`). `plugins/rust-search` and `plugins/chrome-rs` build separately because they need `panic = "unwind"` (see `Cargo.toml`). ### Build Needs Windows x64, Rust stable (1.85+) with the MSVC toolchain. ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\build-all.ps1 ``` Result: `target\release\plugin-launcher.exe`, with every plugin inside. Close a running installer first. Tests: `cargo test --workspace` (and `cargo test` in `plugins\rust-search`). CI runs the same on every push (`.github/workflows/build.yml`). | Script | What it does | |---|---| | `build-all.ps1` | everything: plugins → `payload\` → installer | | `build-plugins.ps1` | plugins only → `payload\` (no installer rebuild) | | `update-plugin.ps1 ` | rebuild and reinstall one installed plugin without rebuilding the installer (asks for admin via UAC) | | `user-mode.ps1`, `dev-update.ps1` | developer mode: run topbar, rust-explorer, rs-shell and reshell from `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on top of Explorer, swap them without admin | | `bench.ps1` | the search and Task Manager benchmark | | `publish.ps1`, `release.ps1` | commit and push; GitHub release with `WinRust.exe` | ### Command line From a terminal **with administrator rights**: ``` plugin-launcher list plugin-launcher install ... --yes (one or more names, or `all` for the default components; without --yes it only prints warnings) plugin-launcher update |all (reinstall from payload\ next to the exe) plugin-launcher uninstall plugin-launcher rollback --yes (remove everything) plugin-launcher autoupdate (one update check now: what the WinRust-update task runs) ``` To include `rust-explorer` in a fresh bulk install, run `plugin-launcher install all rust-explorer --yes`. If `topbar` is already installed, you can install `rust-explorer` on its own. Several plugins in one command are installed in the table's order (topbar before rust-explorer); one that fails does not stop the rest. Exit codes: 0 success, 1 error (at least one plugin failed), 2 bad arguments or no `--yes`. With no arguments the window opens. Install log: `%ProgramData%\plugin-launcher\install.log`. ### Adding a plugin 1. A crate in `plugins/`, added to `members` in the root `Cargo.toml`. 2. A line in `payload.txt`. 3. `src/install/.rs` with an install/uninstall pair (and a `mod` line in `src/install/mod.rs`). Save the original values before changing anything, so uninstall can put them back. 4. An entry in `PLUGINS` (`src/main.rs`). The window, its height and the command line pick it up on their own. ## License Licensed under either of [MIT](LICENSE-MIT) or [Apache-2.0](LICENSE-APACHE) at your option.

items.description: Steer ideas like a space pilot!
items.readme:
# 🕹️ Spaceship IDE

Steer your ideas in realtime, space pilot style!

![Screencast](./extra/screencast.gif)

## Demos

Watch on [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfyQPhFtW-z/) and [YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3WmNLWUmcnY). You can try the simulator at [https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/) with the option to go live with your API keys for Cerebras and Gemini. Keys stay in your browser local storage. Do it at your own risk.

## Conjecture

> In the near future, LLM and Decision Models will reach 60 FPS interactivity.

When that happens, what new interaction paradigms will unlock? This project demonstrates plausible and desirable interactions for that future.

1. **Focus monitor**: can we visualize what LLM is paying attention to, and use that to guide human's focus towards what's important?

   ![focus monitor](./extra/clips/focus-monitor.gif)

2. **Attention lock**: can we force LLM to pay more attention to specific phrases so as to bias its future behavior?

   ![attention lock](./extra/clips/attention-lock.gif)

3. **Future Vector Steering**: can we decompose the task into eigenvectors, independently tune each, and re-compose them to influence the incoming text?

   ![future steering](./extra/clips/future-steering.gif)

4. **Realtime re-generation**: when text generation is cheap and fast, can we explore alternative futures by scrubbing?

   ![realtime regeneration](./extra/clips/realtime-regeneration.gif)

## Design process

I used Claude Code for most of the implementation but stayed hands-on for the UI/UX. I iterate using interactive style swatch, a technique where I prompt AI to give me diverse options of designs, I provide feedback, and it iterates. You can see the design artifacts in the [extra page](https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/extra/style-1.html).

To achieve the realtime experience, I have to use agreesive speculative generation and manage cache invalidation based on user interactions. For example, when the main knob moves backward, I have to empty future texts and cancel ongoing requests. There are many considerations like this throughout the system and that took a lot of human judgement - claude didn't one shot them.

## Theory

I'm currently focusing on systems that help human shape ideas in realtime. This project is a small step towards my [upcoming thesis](https://code.chuanqisun.com/master-thesis/) at the MIT Media Lab, where I investigate how semantic and symoblic systems can be coupled to enhance human creativity, agency, and joy of craft.

## Citation

If you build on this work, please cite it as:

```bibtex
@misc{sun2026spaceship,
  author       = {Sun, Chuanqi},
  title        = {Spaceship {IDE}: Steer Your Ideas in Realtime, Space Pilot Style},
  year         = {2026},
  publisher    = {GitHub},
  howpublished = {\url{https://github.com/chuanqisun/spaceship}},
  note         = {Demo: \url{https://chuanqisun.github.io/spaceship/}}
}
```

items.readme:
# Boring Marketing Skills

Free marketing skills for your AI agent: research, positioning, copy, pages, SEO, AI search, ads, email and content, plus a deep pack for local businesses and the people who market them.

32 skills for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and other agents. They were built from real campaigns, and every one works without a paid tool. MIT licensed.

Made by James Dickerson ([@boringmarketer](https://x.com/boringmarketer)). More at [boringmarketing.com](https://boringmarketing.com). Need clients to use this on? [boringfunnels.com](https://boringfunnels.com) finds local businesses losing customers (I make it). Want agents built for your team? [Work with us](https://boringmarketing.com/#work).

## Install

Any agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others):

```bash
npx skills add boringmarketer/boring-marketing-skills
```

Claude Code plugin:

```
/plugin marketplace add boringmarketer/boring-marketing-skills
/plugin install boring-marketing@boring-marketing-skills
```

Then type `/start-here` and name the business. It reads the site and the reviews, writes the brand files every other skill uses, and tells you which skill to run next. The first run takes about 3 minutes.

## The skills

Grouped by stage, in the order a customer meets a business.

### Start here

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `start-here` | Reads the business (yours or a client's), writes the brand files, and routes you to the next skill |
| `brand-voice` | Pulls the voice from the site and reviews so every page and post sounds like the business |
| `positioning-angles` | Finds the angle and the offer that make them the obvious call |
| `audience-research` | Reads reviews, forums and competitors for the words customers actually use |
| `competitive-intel` | Sizes up the rivals that show up first, including what their customers complain about |

### Get found

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `google-business-profile` | Checks the Google profile against the top 3 in the map pack and writes a month of posts |
| `local-seo-plan` | Decides which services and towns get a page, which get a section, and which to skip |
| `service-area-pages` | Writes town and service pages that aren't the same page with the city swapped |
| `ai-search` | Checks whether ChatGPT, Perplexity and Google's AI name the business, and what to fix if they don't |
| `site-audit` | Crawls the site like Google and the AI crawlers do and ranks the few technical fixes that stop it being found |
| `keyword-research` | Maps what people search, from free autocomplete data, as topics instead of a 5,000-row list |
| `seo-content` | Writes the articles and guides that answer those searches |
| `programmatic-seo` | Builds many pages from one template and a data set, without thin pages |

### Get chosen

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `reviews` | Finds where reviews stall, writes the owner replies, and sets up the ask after every job |
| `first-screen-check` | Looks at the site on a phone the way a customer does: is the number, the promise and the proof on the first screen? |
| `landing-page` | Builds a page for one service and one offer, phone first |
| `direct-response-copy` | Writes headlines, offers and pages that get the call |
| `lead-magnet` | Makes the checklist, quote calculator or guide people trade an email for |

### Get the call

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `paid-ads` | Writes Google and Meta ads and the test plan for them |
| `google-ads-tracking` | Makes Google Ads count calls and form fills, so it bids on real leads |
| `ads-incrementality-check` | Runs a pause test against the phone log to see if the ads make the phone ring or only take credit |
| `meta-ads` | Sets up the Meta API, launches the campaign and proves the tracking fires |
| `speed-to-lead` | Finds missed calls and slow replies, then sets up the text-back and follow-up |
| `creative` | Makes ad images and short videos with AI image and video models |

### Bring them back

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `email-sequences` | Writes the welcome, quote follow-up, review ask and seasonal emails |
| `newsletter` | Plans and writes a newsletter people open |
| `performance-review` | Reads the numbers each month and says what to keep, cut and test |

### Win clients (for agencies and freelancers)

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `find-local-clients` | Picks a trade and a town, then ranks the businesses losing the most customers |
| `pitch-the-fix` | Finds the owner and writes a short email about one thing that's broken, with a fix you can sell |

Every skill can keep a separate folder per client. Tell `/start-here` "new client" and it sets one up.

### Market yourself

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `social-content` | Writes posts from your own best posts, not generic hooks |
| `long-form-article` | Plans and drafts a long guide with real numbers and named sources |
| `content-atomizer` | Turns one piece into posts for every platform |

## Found in the work

These skills came out of real campaigns. Three of the findings behind them:

- **The promise isn't on the page.** Most local businesses running ads that promise 24/7 or same-day service don't say it on the first screen of the page the ad opens (hundreds of local sites checked on a phone, Nov 2026). That's `first-screen-check`.
- **The ads were taking credit.** Google credited a Performance Max campaign with most of an account's conversions. Paused, the phone log didn't move. That's `ads-incrementality-check`.
- **One campaign beat three.** On the same small budget, one broad campaign brought leads at a fraction of the cost of the same money split three ways by city. That's in `paid-ads`.

## What we use

Every skill works with your agent's own web access. When you want more, this is the stack we run, and each skill names the pick at the step where it helps, with the free way first.

| Job | What we use | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Web search for agents | Exa | Free tier, then pay as you go |
| Read, crawl and extract pages | Firecrawl | Free tier |
| Search volumes, SERPs, keyword data | DataForSEO | Pay as you go |
| Images and GIFs | GPT Image 2.6 (OpenAI) | Pay per image |
| Video | Seedance 2.5, through Higgsfield or Replicate | Pay per clip |
| Presenter and UGC-style ad video | Higgsfield Marketing Studio | Plans with credits |
| Voiceover | ElevenLabs | Free tier, then plans |
| Meta ads | Meta's official Ads MCP server and Ads CLI | Free with an ad account |
| Google Ads | Google Ads API | Free |
| Posting and scheduling | Zernio | Plans |
| Many data APIs, one key | treg | Pay per call |
| Search Console, Business Profile | Google | Free |
| Finding local businesses to pitch | boringfunnels (mine) | Free search, paid Pro |

Keys, setup and what each one unlocks: [TOOLS.md](TOOLS.md).

**About boringfunnels.** I make it, so every skill that mentions it says so on the same line. It never replaces the free path, and no skill needs it.

## Work with me

The skills are free. If you want more than the skills:

- **Have it built and run for you.** My team embeds with a few companies at a time and builds goal-tied AI agents that run their marketing. [boringmarketing.com](https://boringmarketing.com)
- **Learn to do it and sell it.** The [Boring Marketing community](https://www.skool.com/the-vibe-marketers) is where I teach marketers and agencies the whole playbook.
- **Find clients to use it on.** [boringfunnels.com](https://boringfunnels.com) finds local businesses losing customers (I make it).
- **Read the guides.** Long breakdowns on X at [@boringmarketer](https://x.com/boringmarketer).

## Updates

New skills land here first. Watch the repo to hear about them, and follow [@boringmarketer](https://x.com/boringmarketer) for the guides.

Found a bug or a skill that gave bad advice? Open an issue with what you asked and what it did.

MIT. Use it for your business, your clients or your own product.
